query: How can support teams reduce ticket resolution time?

per_column.name: issue_category
per_column.rationale: The type of issue affects resolution difficulty/time but is an intrinsic property of the ticket, not a settable lever. It is a common-cause style covariate to adjust for, not an intervenable treatment.

per_column.name: operational_severity
per_column.rationale: Severity of impact is an intrinsic characteristic of the incident that drives resolution time; it can be adjusted for but is not something a team could freely set.

per_column.name: technical_complexity
per_column.rationale: Complexity is an intrinsic property of the problem that strongly influences resolution_minutes; an actor cannot simply set it. Serves as a covariate.

per_column.name: affected_scope
per_column.rationale: Scope of impact is an inherent attribute of the issue influencing resolution effort/time; not intervenable, but adjustable.

per_column.name: requires_escalation
per_column.rationale: Whether/where a ticket is escalated is a downstream operational decision that lies on the causal path between the issue and resolution time; it is arguably an action the team takes but it is a consequence of the issue, so it functions as a mediator rather than a clean exogenous treatment.

per_column.name: root_cause_domain
per_column.rationale: The domain of the root cause is an intrinsic property of the underlying defect affecting resolution time; a covariate, not a lever.

per_column.name: customer_urgency_signal
per_column.rationale: Urgency signals originate from the customer and are exogenous inputs that may correlate with prioritization and resolution time; not team-settable.

per_column.name: workaround_available
per_column.rationale: Availability of a workaround is largely a property of the issue that affects how quickly it can be closed; not a clean intervenable treatment.

per_column.name: data_or_billing_sensitivity
per_column.rationale: Sensitivity is an intrinsic attribute of the ticket influencing handling and time; a covariate, not a lever.

judge.rationale: The query asks an interventional what-if question ('How can support teams reduce resolution time?'), which requires at least one intervenable lever (treatment) plus confounders to adjust for. The added columns are almost entirely intrinsic characteristics of the ticket/issue (category, severity, complexity, scope, root cause, urgency, workaround, sensitivity). These are legitimate, non-obvious confounders not named in the query, so confounder coverage is decent. However, the operator FAILS the decisive interventional test: no column represents a settable, changeable, team-controlled lever. 'requires_escalation' is the closest to an action but is downstream of the issue and functions as a mediator, not an exogenous treatment. With no valid intervenable treatment, the counterfactual effect of any intervention cannot be estimated, so the what-if claim is not satisfied despite good confounder work.
